name: Sovereign Website
kicker: Websites built by agents, owned by you
description: An independent brochure about Sovereign Website: websites built by a team of AI agents and owned by the people they are for, from its own public pages.
headline: Your website, built by agents and owned by you
lede: A team of AI agents builds a static website, shows the owner five designs and hands it over. The files, the history and the address belong to the owner, who can move it anywhere and change it by talking to their own AI.

quote.q: Your website. Built by agents, owned by you.

what.t: A team of AI agents builds a website, shows five designs and hands it over. The files, history and address belong to the owner, who can move it anywhere.
It comes in two forms: an open pattern that anyone can use for free, the way anyone can install WordPress, and a hosted version that is being prepared.
"Sovereign" here means owning the site and being able to move it. The sites say plainly that this "is not a legal or certification claim".
**Status, as the company states it:** "Nothing is sold yet. The hosted service under this name, and the pattern's own repository, do not exist yet."
**What a visitor can do today:** take the "one-minute self-check" on the company's maturity model, which places a website from level 0, "rented", to level 5, "sovereign and proven".

story.t: Sovereign Website began inside AgentiCCells, where sites were first made as "the AgentiCCells website cell" before they had a name of their own.
On 17 November 2026 a change to the AgentiCCells site factory gave the owner's own GitHub account access to the site it built, and one request went from commit to live site in 55 seconds.
Two days later, on 19 November 2026, the sovereignwebsite.ai, .com and .site domains and the SovereignWebsite GitHub organisation were set up, and sovereignwebsite.org was registered the same day.

On 20 November 2026 the first design for sovereignwebsite.ai was chosen, the principles were licensed CC BY 4.0, and a demonstration site was built from a single request, its repository created 43 seconds after the request arrived.

for_whom.t: Small businesses such as "a florist, a bakery or a surf school", who need not know the stack underneath.
People moving off Wix, Squarespace or WordPress.
Partners who would resell it: freelancers, small consultancies and larger firms (a draft programme).
Developers and anyone who wants to use the open pattern themselves.

how.title: Five designs

how.title: The hand-over

how.title: The first change
how.t: The milestone is the owner's first change, made by talking to their own AI.
